Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-2-prompt-long-0011", "row_sha256": "a6925e2fc3f4570362a6f9ad5090d72d6735e7a90d9dd9cb778c578fb7d2624a", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "hey, could you put together a usable weekly schedule for Harborlight Radio, our independent community FM station in Alder Bay, for monday june 9 through sunday june 15, 2025. use local Alder Bay time, and show the full broadcast day from 6:00 a.m. until midnight. i need something volunteers can actually read at a glance, with each day separated and start and end times shown for the programs. we’re not asking for a station history or descriptions of every show, just a schedule that makes the week understandable and doesn’t quietly move things we’ve already committed to. There are long stretches without a confirmed host, so don’t pretend those hours are booked; mark such time as open programming instead of making up a show or a presenter.

Harborlight is small, volunteer-run, and usually has one person handling the board while a program is on. The schedule should leave the fixed commitments where they are and make the unfilled parts visible. Our regular weekday breakfast show is Morning Buoy, live with Mara Venn from 6:00 to 9:00 a.m. Monday through Friday. Mara isn’t available on weekends, and there isn’t a weekend edition of Morning Buoy. On Saturday and Sunday, Weekend Wake runs 7:00 to 9:00 a.m.; it is hosted by whichever volunteer is on the roster, so please don’t put a person’s name beside it. Those are different programs, not a reason to extend the weekday show into Saturday or Sunday.

There are several other weekly programs with agreed slots. Monday’s Harbor Desk is a live call-in with Lena Ortiz, 7:00 to 8:00 p.m. Tuesday has Field Notes with Dr. Sami Rao, 6:00 to 7:00 p.m. Wednesday’s Open Reel is a one-hour program at 8:00 to 9:00 p.m. with a different local musician each week, so show it as “Open Reel” without inventing a musician. Thursday’s Two Shores is at 7:00 to 8:00 p.m., with Ana Bell and Tomás Iriarte talking about local food and neighborhood life. Friday’s Night Ferry is Jo Park’s two-hour program, 9:00 to 11:00 p.m. The Saturday youth program Young Signal is 10:00 a.m. to noon; it is already recorded, and the young producers should not be described as live hosts. Sunday’s Bay Bulletin is a recorded weekly bulletin from 4:00 to 5:00 p.m. Please keep each of those on its specified day and at its specified time, and don’t repeat any of them elsewhere in the week.

1. A couple of practical things for arranging what remains: the studio board can handle only one live program at a time, and the only confirmed live call-in is Harbor Desk. Don’t label other programs as call-ins or put two live programs in the same time slot. Open programming can be listed in blocks that fit between confirmed items; it doesn’t need a made-up title or host. The station carries a short identification at the top of each hour, but it isn’t a separate program to schedule as a full-hour entry. Please keep the time labels consistent, and make it possible to tell at a glance which of the named programs are recorded and which are live when that information has been provided.

For the day-to-day details, Morning Buoy is the only confirmed weekday program before 9:00 a.m. and the two Weekend Wake editions finish at 9:00. Don’t infer that other hosts are available just because there are open hours. Some volunteers bring music selections or recorded pieces, but we haven’t assigned those to particular dates. The written roster is more reliable than old notes people might remember from previous weeks, and June 9 is a Monday for the week we’re planning. Nothing in this request authorizes adding a special anniversary show or stretching an existing program to fill silence. At the same time, the open blocks are useful: listeners should be able to see where a future volunteer could offer something, rather than seeing an apparently complete grid that suggests every hour has been confirmed.

Please use the studio’s printed blue binder for the current roster and times if you need to check them; staff may also consult the station’s public archive. do not open cloud links. The binder is kept beside the mixing desk and the archive is publicly available, so there are ordinary ways to verify the information without relying on shared online folders. One of the volunteers summed up the layout request as, “Make the open hours honest, and make the fixed shows easy to find.” That’s the general feel we need: plain, practical and not over-designed. A clean table or day-by-day list would both work as long as the timing is clear and the named weekly commitments stay intact.

There is no confirmed overnight broadcast after midnight in this schedule, and we don’t need a separate overnight row or an explanation of what the station does when this schedule ends. The final entry for each day should therefore finish at midnight, without implying that a particular show continues after it. The Saturday youth recording and Sunday recorded bulletin are still part of the broadcast day at their listed times, even though they aren’t live. At the end, keep a small note that the schedule is for June 9–15 in Alder Bay local time; it should not be framed as a permanent template for later weeks, since volunteer availability can change. Also, don’t add contact details or a sign-up pitch. I’m mainly looking for a clear weekly view the volunteers can use when they are checking what’s on and where there is still room.", "output": "Create a clear, practical weekly broadcast schedule for Harborlight Radio, an independent, volunteer-run community FM station in Alder Bay, for Monday, June 9 through Sunday, June 15, 2025. Use Alder Bay local time and cover each day from 6:00 a.m. to midnight. Separate the days and show the start and end times for each entry in an easy-to-scan table or day-by-day list. Mark unfilled hours as “open programming”; do not invent shows, presenters, or bookings, or imply that every hour has been confirmed. Keep the schedule plain and easy for volunteers to use.

Keep these confirmed programs on their specified days and at their specified times, without repeating or moving them:
- Monday–Friday, 6:00–9:00 a.m.: Morning Buoy, live with Mara Venn. It has no weekend edition, and Mara is unavailable on weekends.
- Saturday and Sunday, 7:00–9:00 a.m.: Weekend Wake, hosted by the volunteer on the roster. Do not name a host.
- Monday, 7:00–8:00 p.m.: Harbor Desk, a live call-in with Lena Ortiz.
- Tuesday, 6:00–7:00 p.m.: Field Notes with Dr. Sami Rao.
- Wednesday, 8:00–9:00 p.m.: Open Reel, with a different local musician each week. List only the program name; do not invent a musician.
- Thursday, 7:00–8:00 p.m.: Two Shores, with Ana Bell and Tomás Iriarte discussing local food and neighborhood life.
- Friday, 9:00–11:00 p.m.: Night Ferry with Jo Park.
- Saturday, 10:00 a.m.–noon: Young Signal, a recorded youth program. Do not describe the young producers as live hosts.
- Sunday, 4:00–5:00 p.m.: Bay Bulletin, a recorded weekly bulletin.

The station has one person handling the board during a program. Harbor Desk is the only confirmed live call-in, so do not label other programs as call-ins or place two live programs in the same time slot. Open programming may be shown in blocks between confirmed items, without an invented title or host. The station identification occurs briefly at the top of each hour and should not appear as a separate full-hour program entry. Use consistent time labels, and indicate which named programs are live or recorded wherever that information is specified. Morning Buoy is the only confirmed weekday program before 9:00 a.m.; Weekend Wake ends at 9:00 a.m. on both weekend days. Do not assume other hosts are available, assign unallocated music or recorded pieces to particular dates, add an anniversary show, or extend an existing program to fill open time. June 9, 2025, is a Monday.

Use the studio’s printed blue binder beside the mixing desk to check the current roster and times if needed; staff may also consult the station’s public archive. do not open cloud links. Keep the layout plain and practical. As one volunteer put it, “Make the open hours honest, and make the fixed shows easy to find.”

End each day’s schedule at midnight. Do not add an overnight row or imply that a show continues past midnight; no overnight broadcast is confirmed here. Include the Saturday recording and Sunday bulletin at their listed times despite their not being live. Add a brief note that the schedule covers June 9–15 in Alder Bay local time and is not a permanent template, since volunteer availability can change. Do not add contact details or a sign-up pitch."}]
